data.name: Method_Catalogue
data.value: Catalogue {0} {1} of {2}: rules: {3}, of which checks: {4} and inventory rules: {5}. All rule texts are Riegel's own.

data.name: Method_Collection
data.value: Riegel's collector reads the machine's configuration and runtime state – registry, security policy, audit policy, services, Defender, firewall, BitLocker, local accounts – without changing anything and without network access, and writes a snapshot of raw facts with its SHA-256. The evaluation checks the snapshot offline against the rule catalogue and applies the plant's registers. Administrator rights extend what can be read; without them the affected rules are reported as not checkable.

data.name: Method_Evidence_1
data.value: “Met” only with positive evidence: missing, denied, truncated or uncollected data gives “not checkable”, never “met”.

data.name: Method_Evidence_2
data.value: A value that is not set counts only where the collection covered that part completely; a default value is used only with a cited source and flagged “Default value assumed”.

data.name: Method_Evidence_3
data.value: Runtime evidence beats configuration: where Windows reports the effective state (SMB, LSA protection, firewall, Defender, VBS), that state decides; a configured-only value is never “met”.

data.name: Method_Evidence_4
data.value: A value of the wrong type is “not met”; heuristic evidence alone (for example the security center entry of a third-party antivirus) is “not checkable”.

data.name: Method_Evidence_5
data.value: A missing protection is a gap (“not met”, with the route to an exception), not “not applicable”.

data.name: Method_Evidence_6
data.value: Below 90% checkable or without administrator rights, the report carries the banner “Incomplete check” and the values are shown in grey.

data.name: Method_Limit_1
data.value: No compliance statement: Riegel supports evidence for the frameworks named on the cover; it does not certify conformity.

data.name: Method_Limit_2
data.value: Not a GMP validation package: the report is a human-reviewed input to periodic review and change control.

data.name: Method_Limit_3
data.value: What the machine cannot show is not checked: MFA, backups, network segmentation, incident handling and physical security.

data.name: Method_Limit_4
data.value: The result describes the state at collection time; later changes are visible only in a new run.

data.name: Method_NoCisBsi
data.value: This report and the catalogue contain no CIS or BSI content: no texts, values or IDs from CIS Benchmarks, BSI SiSyPHuS or IT-Grundschutz modules, and no files or values from Microsoft security baselines. Grundschutz++ appears as identifiers only.

data.name: Method_Provenance
data.value: Provenance of the expected values (rules: {0}): ACSC {1}, Microsoft Windows Server documentation (CC BY 4.0) {2}, Microsoft Learn facts {3}, DISA {4}; also found in a Microsoft security baseline (corroboration only): {5}.

data.name: Method_Score
data.value: Weights: high 3, medium 2, low 1, over the checkable results (met, not met, deliberately open). Hardening level = weighted met ÷ checkable; documented = (met + deliberately open) ÷ checkable. Exceptions never raise the hardening level; tailoring removes the rule from both values. The audit category contributes at most 12 weight points. Checked share = checkable ÷ (applicable − out of scope − inventory). Rounded at the end, half away from zero. Domain controllers get no hardening level.

data.name: Score_Explained
data.value: Hardening level: weighted share of met rules among the checkable ones (high 3, medium 2, low 1). Documented: met plus deliberately open. Checked share: checkable among the applicable rules in scope.
